tables.title: Blob use steps for signing public key computation (CCOP = 0b10000001)
tables.text: Table 191, "Blob use steps for signing public key computation (CCOP = 0b10000001)", in section 25.5.2 (ECDSA signature) on page 761. Columns: OPSTEP, inM OPDKEA, iGn CSMAPEHS, Coupling or chaining operations, End-step (1)event, CPU action. 10 data row(s). Notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform described event for CCB to automatically go to the next step.; 2. SAES cannot be used for any operations, for security reasons.

rows:
–Enable the PKA in the correct mode, writing in PKA_CR 
MODE= 0x20 and EN=1 (repeat if EN bit stays clear). 
Wait for INITOK=1 in PKA_SR.
–Optionally decrypt blob encryption key in the SAES, 
using DHUK in 256-bit wrapped key mode.
–Set up AES-GCM in decryption mode with DHUK or the 
decrypted key in register (if applicable).

–Complete GCM initialization in decryption mode, using 
saved random IV.
–Write reference tag in CCB_REFTAGR.

Write ECC signature parameters in the PKA RAM, 
clearing CCF flags in SAES, triggered after each2x32-bit 
write.

–Write encrypted d in SAES DINR and run AES 
decryption round.
–Write incrementallyscalar multiplier k in the PKA, using 
0xCCB magic number. 
–Repeat for each 16 bytes block of data.

–Complete GCM final.
–Read computed tag in the SAES (returns 0).
Start the operation in PKA setting START bit in PKA_CR.
The PKA computes the operation. PKA RAM is read as0.
–Read public key point Q in PKA RAM

–Read public key point Q in PKA RAM
–Set IPRST in CCB

Clear the IPRST bit in CCB when CCB_BUSY and 
OPSTEP are cleared in CCB_SR. 
Before writing new ECDSA signature blob in non-volatile 
memory do the following:
–Enable the PKA in the correct mode, writing in PKA_CR 
MODE= 0x26 and EN=1. Wait for INITOK=1.
–Write the hash z used during blob creation (see 
Table189)
–Write ECDSA verification parameters in PKA, including 
the public key coordinates computed in step 0x1A.
–Start the operation setting START bit in PKA_CR
–Wait for PROCENDF bit is set. If the signature is valid 
save the created blob in non-volatile memory.
notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform described event for CCB to automatically go to the next step.
2. SAES cannot be used for any operations, for security reasons.
